title: Ang 631–634: Guru Tegh Bahadur in Sorath
tomorrow: why would a hymn take so many stanzas to say one thing?

cards: Five days before a wedding, the photographer cancels, and the group chat goes from hearts to all caps in under a minute. Everybody is either panicking or pretending not to care.
Guru Tegh Bahadur, on ang 633, describes a third way of being, and it answers yesterday's question. The one who feels pain, and doesn't take it as pain.

teach.b: The ninth Guru's hymns in Sorath are short, and this one is a portrait.

teach.h: GOLD AS DUST; PRAISE AND BLAME ALIKE.
teach.b: In paraphrase: the one who, in pain, doesn't count it as pain; who isn't bound by pleasure, attachment or fear, and sees gold as dust.

Slander and praise don't sway them, nor greed or pride; they stay apart from joy and sorrow, honor and dishonor. Nanak says, such a one merges with God like water into water. Notice what the hymn doesn't say.
It never says the pain isn't there, or that nothing matters. The person still feels it. They just aren't run by it, not by the bad news and not by the good.
That's the difference between unmoved and numb: numb shuts the door on feeling; unmoved lets it in and keeps its seat. Look closely, and the same hymn puts praise next to slander.
Being unmoved isn't only about bearing bad days. It's about not being run by compliments, either.

how: Guru Tegh Bahadur's Sorath hymns are read and sung in kirtan; this portrait of the one 'unmoved by pain' is often recited when Sikhs speak of steadiness in hard times.

games.q: the ninth Guru's portrait — tap the pairs.
p: felt, but not taken as pain

s: the hymn never says the pain isn't there; the person isn't run by it.
the same hymn puts praise next to slander
neither one sways the person Guru Tegh Bahadur describes.
this hymn is about bearing bad days only
joy and sorrow, honor and dishonor: good news doesn't run them either.

games.q: you just got great news and terrible news on the same afternoon. what does the ninth Guru's portrait look like right now?
o: feel both fully, and let neither one take the wheel.
push both feelings down until you feel nothing at all.
lean into the good news so the bad one hurts less.
games.why: the portrait stays apart from joy and sorrow alike. unmoved means not ruled, not numb.

practice: Close your eyes and sit still. When a sensation comes, an itch, an ache, a pleasant warmth, name it quietly, pleasant or unpleasant, and let it be there without chasing it or pushing it off.
Let both kinds come and go for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: Ang 631. Where Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns in Sorath begin, and two pages on, the one who isn't ruled by pain or praise.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru; his hymns are headed Mahala 9.

carryVoice: Your line: unmoved, which isn't numb. You still feel it; it just doesn't drive. Sorath keeps going next week.
